news.title: US stocks rose near record levels after latest jobs report eased worries
news.text:
US stocks climbed near their all-time high on Friday after the latest update on the U.S. job market cooled worries that a potentially hot U.S economy could make inflation much worse. 

The S&P 500 rose 0.7 per cent and pulled within 1.0 per cent of its record set in August. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 250 points, or 0.5 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite gained 1.2per cent.

All of Wall Street got a jolt after the U.S. government said employers across the country added 29,000 more jobs to their payrolls than they cut last month. That was fewer than economists expected and a slowdown from August’s net hiring rate of 133,000.

More importantly for financial markets, it tamped down concerns that the U.S. economy could be so strong that it could fuel inflation even higher. Inflation has remained much worse than anyone would like, and the Federal Reserve recently raised its main interest rate for the first time in three years to try to rein in the painful increases for the cost of living. 

Encouraging signs of easing inflation gave markets a boost.Even though Americans are feeling more frustrated about inflation and their finances, the overall U.S. economy has been chugging along. Earlier this week, the U.S. government said the economy’s growth in the spring was better than earlier thought, driven by businesses building AI data centres and spending by consumers. 

Friday’s softer-than-expected data on the economy pushed traders to pare bets the Fed will hike its main interest rate at its next meeting later this month. They now see less than a 23per cent probability of that, down from 64per cent a week ago, according to data from CME Group. 

“This report strengthens the case for the Federal Reserve to remain patient,” according to Adam Schickling, senior economist at Vanguard. “The labour market has not deteriorated sharply, but there is also little evidence that it has meaningfully strengthened, giving policymakers reason to wait for additional data.”

The pullback in expectations for an October rate hike helped calm what’s been a rattled bond market.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury briefly dropped all the way below 5.17per cent. That was down from its peak near 5.35per cent on Thursday, when it and other longer-term yields neared their highest levels in two decades.

An easing of yields can help the economy by making it more affordable for everyone to borrow money. Higher yields, meanwhile, tend to undercut prices for stocks and other investments. 

But a solid U.S. economy is only one of the many drivers that have caused yields to jump in bond markets. 

Oil prices yo-yoed in another shaky day, and the price of a barrel of Brent oil veered between US$98 and US$103 on Friday. It ended up settling at US$102.25, down 0.1per cent, for its latest zigzag amid uncertainty how the war with Iran will reshape the global oil industry. 

As oil prices pared their losses through Friday, so did Treasury yields. The 10-year Treasury yield bounced back to 5.28per cent, more than 0.10 percentage points above its bottom for the day. That in turn helped U.S. stocks pare their own gains. The S&P 500 had been up as much as 1.2 per cent at one point in the morning.

Concerns about big spending by governments, along with the mountains of debt they’re racking up, meanwhile continue to keep yields high worldwide. In France, for example, yields have been particularly shaky as the government contends with its record debt and strained budget. 

On Wall Street, Tesla rallied 4.7 per cent after the electric-vehicle company said it delivered 486,532 vehicles to customers during the latest quarter, more than analysts expected.

Lower yields in the bond market help investors justify paying higher prices for stocks, even those that get criticised for being too expensive. That helped companies in the artificial-intelligence industry add to their already stellar gains.

Nvidia’s 1.3 per cent rise was the single strongest force lifting the S&P 500. Its status as the most valuable company in the U.S. market gives its stock’s movements more influence on the index than others.

Such gains more than made up for a 3.6 per cent drop for Nike. The sneaker and athletic apparel company reported a stronger profit for the latest quarter than analysts expected, but its revenue weakened by more than feared. Nike also gave a forecast for profit this fiscal year that fell short of analysts’ expectations.

All told, the S&P 500 rose 56.27 points to 7,722.72. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 250.40 to 51,176.96, and the Nasdaq composite jumped 319.27 to 27,190.86.

In stock markets abroad, indexes in Europe bounced back from losses taken a day earlier after bond yields swung sharply across the continent. 

Asian indexes were mixed, with Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropping 2.6per cent but South Korea’s Kospi adding 0.5 per cent.

news.title: KOTIN Gaming PC With RTX 5060 Ti Now $1,300 (Save $100)
news.text:
What You Get: Ryzen 7 8700F and RTX 5060 Ti at a $100 Discount

The KOTIN Gaming PC Desktop is now available for $1,299.99, down from its regular $1,399.99 price. At its core, you're getting an AMD Ryzen 7 8700F processor—an 8-core chip designed for gaming and multitasking—paired with an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti graphics card with 8GB of VRAM. The system includes 16GB of DDR5 RAM and a 1TB SSD for storage.

Suggested Reading

Key specifications:

Related Content

AMD Ryzen 7 8700F (8-core processor)NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (8GB VRAM)16GB DDR5 memory1TB SSD storageCurrently $1,299.99 (regular price $1,399.99)

This configuration sits squarely in the entry-level gaming desktop category. The Ryzen 7 8700F provides enough processing power for current games and everyday tasks, while the RTX 5060 Ti brings dedicated graphics performance that integrated solutions can't match. For someone who wants to start gaming immediately without building their own PC, the $100 discount makes this combination more accessible—but only if you understand where it excels and where it falls short.

1080p Gaming Performance: Where This PC Shines

The RTX 5060 Ti with 8GB VRAM is built for 1080p gaming, and that's where this desktop will give you the most consistent experience. At 1920x1080 resolution, you can expect smooth performance in esports titles, popular multiplayer games, and most current single-player releases when you adjust settings appropriately.

For competitive games like Valorant, Counter-Strike 2, and Fortnite, this system will deliver high frame rates at medium-to-high settings. In more demanding titles, you'll get playable frame rates by balancing graphics quality with performance—think high settings rather than ultra, with selective use of ray tracing features.

The 8-core Ryzen 7 8700F complements the GPU well at this resolution, providing enough CPU horsepower to avoid bottlenecks in most gaming scenarios. The combination delivers the "good enough to start gaming today" experience: you'll be able to play what you want at 1080p without constant compromises, as long as you're realistic about settings and understand the VRAM constraint.

The 8GB VRAM Reality: Games and Settings That Will Push the Limits

Here's where transparency matters: the RTX 5060 Ti's 8GB of VRAM is a limitation you need to understand before buying. While 8GB is adequate for many games at 1080p, some titles and settings will expose this bottleneck.

Independent testing from TechSpot has identified severe frame-time issues in VRAM-demanding games like The Last of Us Part II and Horizon Forbidden West on the RTX 5060 Ti 8GB. These stutters occur when games exceed available video memory, forcing data to shuffle between the GPU and system RAM. You'll encounter similar problems in other titles that use high-resolution textures, extensive ray tracing, or detailed open worlds at maximum settings.

For 1440p gaming, the situation becomes more situational. Tom's Hardware testing shows the 8GB version of the RTX 5060 Ti delivers a good 1080p experience but falls behind its 16GB counterpart at higher resolutions and settings, particularly in ray-tracing scenarios. You can play some games at 2560x1440, but you'll need to reduce graphics quality, disable or limit ray tracing, and potentially use upscaling technologies like DLSS. Whether that's acceptable depends on your expectations and which games you play.

The bottom line: this GPU is optimized for 1080p. If you're primarily gaming at that resolution and willing to adjust settings when needed, the 8GB VRAM is workable. If you're planning to play at 1440p frequently or want maximum texture quality in every title, this constraint will frustrate you.

What We Don't Know: The Component Quality Question

This is where buying a prebuilt from a lesser-known brand requires accepting some uncertainty. No detailed information is available about several components that significantly impact system reliability and longevity:

Motherboard model and features (expansion slots, upgrade path, VRM quality)Power supply wattage and efficiency rating (critical for stability and future GPU upgrades)Cooling solution (stock cooler performance, noise levels, thermal headroom)Case quality (build materials, airflow design, cable management)

These aren't trivial details. A cheap power supply can cause system instability or fail prematurely. Inadequate cooling means thermal throttling and increased component wear. A motherboard with limited expansion options restricts future upgrades.

KOTIN also lacks the established reputation and support track record of major prebuilt brands like Dell, HP, or CyberPowerPC. If something goes wrong, you're relying on Amazon's return policy and whatever warranty KOTIN provides—verify both carefully before purchasing. There's limited independent testing or long-term reliability data available for this specific system.

Can You Upgrade Later? RAM, Storage, and Expansion Considerations

The 16GB of DDR5 RAM included in this system is adequate for gaming-focused use, but it sits at the lower end of what's recommended for modern games and multitasking. Some current titles benefit from 32GB, and future releases may demand more.

Before buying, confirm:

Whether the 16GB uses one or two memory modules (dual-channel configuration is significantly faster)How many RAM slots the motherboard hasThe maximum supported memory capacityWhether additional RAM modules are readily available and compatible

The 1TB SSD provides reasonable storage for your operating system and a modest game library. Most modern games range from 50GB to over 150GB installed, so you'll fill this faster than you might expect. Check whether the system has:

Additional M.2 slots for more NVMe storageSATA ports for adding 2.5" SSDs or hard drivesAccessible drive bays for physical installation

The GPU upgrade path is constrained by the unknown power supply. The RTX 5060 Ti is relatively efficient, but a more powerful card would require confirming adequate wattage and appropriate power connectors. Without knowing the PSU specifications, you can't confidently plan for future graphics upgrades.

How This Compares to Building Your Own PC at $1,300

At $1,299.99, this prebuilt occupies an interesting price point. Building an equivalent system yourself would typically include:

AMD Ryzen 7 8700F or similar CPU: ~$230-250RTX 5060 Ti 8GB: ~$400-45016GB DDR5 RAM: ~$60-801TB NVMe SSD: ~$70-90Motherboard: ~$100-150Power supply: ~$60-100Case: ~$60-100Windows license (if needed): ~$100-140

Depending on component selection and current market prices, a DIY build with known-quality parts could cost roughly the same or slightly more, especially if you factor in the operating system. The prebuilt saves you assembly time and provides immediate usability, while building yourself gives you complete control over component quality and specifications.

The value proposition here depends on your priorities. If your time is limited and you want to start gaming today, the prebuilt's convenience has worth. If you value knowing exactly what's inside your PC and want to ensure quality components throughout, building or choosing a prebuilt from an established brand makes more sense, even at a higher cost.

Who Should Buy This (and Who Should Wait)

Consider this KOTIN gaming PC if you:

Primarily play games at 1080p and don't plan to move to 1440p or 4K soonWant a ready-to-use gaming desktop without the time investment of building your ownUnderstand and accept the 8GB VRAM limitation and are willing to adjust settings when necessaryAre comfortable with uncertainty about power supply, motherboard, and cooling component qualityCan verify the exact configuration, included operating system, and return policy before purchasing

Wait or look elsewhere if you:

Plan to game at 1440p regularly or want maximum graphics settings in VRAM-demanding titlesNeed a system you can confidently upgrade with a more powerful GPU in the near futureRequire 32GB of RAM for multitasking, content creation, or specific gamesWant the peace of mind that comes with established brand support and documented component qualityCan build your own PC or afford a prebuilt from a manufacturer with a proven track record

This desktop delivers on its core promise: solid 1080p gaming performance at a $100 discount. It's "good enough to start gaming today" rather than a future-proof investment. If those parameters align with your needs and you're comfortable with the trade-offs, the KOTIN represents accessible entry into PC gaming. Just verify the details and understand the limitations before you buy.

news.title: Nvidia on fire again after massive $1 trn wipe out recently - what’s boosting stock of world’s most valuable company
news.text: Nvidia is back in the spotlight after a sharp recovery from a brutal two-month sell-off that erased more than $1 trillion from the world’s most valuable company’s market capitalisation.The chipmaker’s shares surged as much as 3% on Friday, briefly touching an intraday record high of $237.88 per share on NASDAQ, before paring gains and ending 1.3% higher at $233.95.The latest rally has taken Nvidia shares about 23% higher from their late-July low, when concerns around the outlook for artificial intelligence weighed heavily on the stock. Friday’s move also brought the shares close to their previous record high from May, although they ultimately finished just below that level.The tech stock also soared 45% from its 52-week low of $164.27, hit in May 2026.Nvidia’s market value now stands at roughly $5.6 trillion, putting the company less than $400 billion away from the $6 trillion mark. If reached, that would make Nvidia the first company in history to achieve the milestone.The recovery comes after investor sentiment towards the AI trade shifted sharply over the past few months. Questions around the huge amounts being spent on AI infrastructure had weighed on the stock, raising concerns about whether the spending spree could continue at its current pace.Nvidia stock performanceNvidia’s shares have gained about 25% so far this year, putting the company on course for its fourth consecutive year of double-digit returns. The latest recovery has therefore helped Nvidia regain much of the ground lost during the sell-off and restored investor enthusiasm around the stock.Meanwhile, it has also given strong returns in the near term, soaring 20% in 3 months and 32% in 6 months. In the last 5 years, the US tech stock has given multibagger returns, jumping over 1000%AI agents fuel fresh optimism around Nvidia stockOne of the key factors supporting Nvidia’s latest rebound has been renewed optimism that the next stage of artificial intelligence could generate additional demand for semiconductors.Investors have increasingly focused on AI agents, which can perform tasks with greater autonomy. Developments such as Meta Platforms’ Muse have added to expectations that the growing use of AI agents could translate into higher demand for the computing power required to run them.That has helped shift the focus back towards Nvidia’s position in the AI ecosystem after concerns about excessive spending had dominated the stock’s narrative.However, the company’s enormous valuation also means that developments in the AI industry continue to have an outsized impact on its shares. Any change in expectations around AI infrastructure spending can quickly translate into large moves in Nvidia’s market value.$150 billion buyback gives Nvidia stock another boostAnother major catalyst for Nvidia’s latest rally has been the company’s decision to significantly expand its share buyback programme.On September 28, 2026, Nvidia’s Board of Directors approved a historic $150 billion increase in its ongoing share buyback programme, taking the company’s total remaining repurchase authorisation to $235 billion through fiscal 2028.It is the largest single increase in a buyback authorisation in corporate history, surpassing Apple’s previous record of $110 billion approved in 2024. The move comes as Nvidia’s revenues from its data centre and AI infrastructure businesses continue to surge, with quarterly revenue crossing $96 billion.CEO Jensen Huang said Nvidia’s strong cash-generation capacity allows the company to invest aggressively in next-generation technologies while also returning substantial amounts of capital to shareholders.The buyback announcement provided another reason for investors to remain positive on Nvidia, alongside optimism around future semiconductor demand from AI applications.The company has also sought to address growing concerns around AI safety. Nvidia unveiled a new double-layered AI security system designed to prevent AI agents from operating outside their intended boundaries.Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only. Please consult with an investment advisor before making any investment decisions.
news.author: Pranati Deva

news.title: Nvidia falls short of May record as value nears $6 trn
news.text: Nvidia Corp. shares touched an intraday high for the first time since May before trimming those gains and closing just short of a record as investors piled back into the stock after a two-month selloff that wiped out more than $1 trillion of market value.Shares of the world’s most valuable public company gained as much as 3% Friday to touch an intraday record and closed up 1.3%, shy of their May high. The stock’s rise extended a 23% rally from a late July low when fears surrounding the outlook for artificial intelligence pressured the chip developer’s stock.The rally has been buoyed in recent weeks by optimism that AI agents like Meta Platforms Inc.’s Muse could drive increased demand for semiconductors. Shares got a further boost after Nvidia announced Monday that it was increasing the size of its buyback plan by a record $150 billion.Nvidia’s rebound comes after months of quickly shifting sentiment around the state of the AI landscape, including questions over the hundreds of billions of dollars being spent by firms on its infrastructure and safety risks that the technology could pose to humanity.The Santa Clara, California-based company unveiled a new double-layered AI security system on Monday, meant to stop AI agents from going awry. Nvidia said the new system would have stopped the recent breach of Hugging Face by OpenAI’s models — at a time when investors have become more concerned with AI safety.All told, Nvidia shares have gained about 25% so far this year, on track for their fourth consecutive year of double-digit returns. Its market capitalization now stands at roughly $5.6 trillion, leaving it less than $400 billion away from becoming the first company in history to hit the $6 trillion level.

news.title: Is a Microsoft Stock Split Coming After 23 Years?
news.text:
Microsoft (MSFT +0.92%) stock sat around $518 as of this writing, within about 5% of its record close of $542 set last October.

Microsoft's board rarely let the share price go anywhere near that high before. The software giant split its stock nine times over its first 17 years as a public company, and one share bought at its March 1986 initial public offering is now 288 shares.

But the last split was a 2-for-1 split that took effect in February 2003. The shares have gone from around $25 just after that split to over $500 now.

And Microsoft hasn't announced any plan to split them again. The call is up to the board.

After 23 years without one, could a 10th split be close?

Microsoft used to split well below today's price

Microsoft's board used to split the shares nearly as soon as they got pricey. The first eight splits happened between 1987 and 1999, and every time the stock closed somewhere between around $98 and $178 right before the split took effect.

The 2003 split was the odd one out, at a pre-split price of about $48. And a long flat spell followed. Microsoft shares didn't close back over $50 until October 2015, more than 12 years later. They first cleared $100 in June 2018 and crossed $178, their highest pre-split price of the 1990s, in February 2020.

Put another way, the stock has traded above every price at which Microsoft ever decided to split for most of the past six years, and it's now at almost three times the highest one. If the old pattern still held, I think the board would've split the shares again years ago.

That climb has come with a far bigger business. Showing how much the company keeps growing, Microsoft's fiscal 2026 revenue (for the year ended June 30) rose 18% to $331.8 billion -- a pickup from 15% growth in fiscal 2025 and 16% in fiscal 2024. And non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share grew 22% to $17.28.

Pricier peers

Sure, a few of Microsoft's big tech peers have split their shares lately. Nvidia (NVDA +1.34%) announced a 10-for-1 split in May 2024, Broadcom (AVGO +3.35%) announced its own 10-for-1 split a month later, and Netflix (NFLX -1.16%) announced one in October 2025.

But these stocks were much more expensive than Microsoft's is now. Nvidia closed at around $950 the day of its announcement, Netflix at about $1,090, and Broadcom at about $1,500. All three said the split was at least partly about making their shares more accessible to employees.

Microsoft's share price is a bit over half Nvidia's price the day it announced its split, and around a third of Broadcom's. Next to the companies that did split, Microsoft's stock arguably isn't all that expensive per share.

Also, fractional shares can make the price tag matter less than it used to. Fidelity, for example, lets investors buy a piece of a share of Nasdaq- and NYSE-listed stocks for as little as $1.

What would a split do to Microsoft's Dow weight?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +0.49%) is price-weighted, so a stock's influence on the index depends on its share price, not its market value. This makes Microsoft a heavyweight. By my math, it accounts for about 6% of the index now, the third-biggest weight after Goldman Sachs and Caterpillar.

A split would lower that weight. A 2-for-1 split like Microsoft's last one would cut it to about 3%, which is still near the middle of the pack.

But a 10-for-1 split like Nvidia's might send Microsoft close to the bottom of the index. The shares would trade at about $52, above only Nike among the Dow's 30 stocks, and Microsoft's weight would drop to about 0.6%.

Verizon Communications was only about 0.5% of the Dow when it was removed from the index in June. In its announcement, S&P Dow Jones Indices, which runs the Dow, said that stocks with persistently low prices have an immaterial effect on the Dow.

Is a split coming, then? I doubt one is close. The board has let the shares trade over all of its earlier split prices for most of the last six years, and $518 is modest next to where Nvidia, Broadcom, and Netflix split. If a split does come sometime, I'd expect a small one, more like the 2-for-1 splits in Microsoft's past than a 10-for-1.

Either way, a split wouldn't change what buyers pay for the business. At around 30 times adjusted earnings, I think the stock's priced about right for a company that grew adjusted earnings per share 22% last fiscal year.
news.summary: The software giant split its shares nine times over its first 17 years as a public company. Is a 10th split on the way?
news.author: Daniel Sparks
